title: Intel Arc GPUs
subtitle: An Intel Arc Pro GPU is ActiveKV's home: a 27B model serving 128,000-token histories on one 32 GB card, kernel patches on a new architecture, and a published quantization built for it.

stats.label: patches to Intel's own kernel sources, each with identical outputs
more sustained throughput, all-4-bit against a mixed 4-bit and 8-bit control
higher perplexity paid for that throughput, eight-document diagnostic set

lede: ActiveKV: I wanted a 27B hybrid model to serve long contexts on one 32 GB card. On a 32 GB Intel Arc Pro GPU the key-value cache was the wall, and I chose to make that card the target and fix the stack where it fell short. ActiveKV keeps attention history in pinned host memory and gives the card a bounded working set, so a 4-bit-weight build of a 27-billion-parameter hybrid recurrent-attention open-weight model serves histories from 32K tokens upward on a single card.
quote: Every kernel patch had to produce identical outputs before I took any speed from it.
evidence: Intel GPU and SYCL/oneAPI engineering: Intel kernel sources patched on Xe2 with identical outputs, cold 32K-token prefill cut from 21.54 s to 17.23 s and recurrent prefill from 53.8 to 27.4 ms per chunk.
LLM quantization (4-bit): a calibration-free W4A16 build taking a 27B hybrid model from 55.6 GB to 20.6 GB for one 32 GB card, about 36% more throughput for 3.33% higher perplexity.
GPU inference optimisation: an 8,000-token request at 3.68 s to first token and 43.3 ms per token, against 4.71 s and 45.3 ms for stock vLLM on the same Intel Arc Pro card.
Profiling methodology: a trace conclusion about copy and compute overlap retracted after a controlled experiment showed the timing events themselves serialised the copy engine.
author: Corey James
